question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,[\operatorname{arcsch}⁡({x}^{2}+4)-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{|{x}^{2}+4|\sqrt{1+{({x}^{2}+4)}^{2}}}\cdot {({x}^{2}+4)}^{′}-\frac{{({x}^{2}+4)}^{′}}{{x}^{2}+4} \\  & =-\frac{1}{({x}^{2}+4)\sqrt{1+({x}^{4}+8{x}^{2}+16)}}\cdot 2x-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4} \\  & =-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+4)\sqrt{{x}^{4}+8{x}^{2}+17}}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4} \\  & =-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{4}+8{x}^{2}+17}}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
